question: Why are DRF drug prices kept lower than regular commercial pharmacies?

options.A: To ensure low-income patients can afford essential treatments
options.B: To punish private pharmacy owners for overcharging people
options.C: To make patients buy more drugs than they actually need
options.D: To drive private pharmaceutical companies completely out of business

explanation: Exactly! Public hospitals use DRFs to protect everyday people from suffering or extreme poverty just because they need basic medicine.

question: A woman in labor is having strong contractions. Which part of her uterine wall is doing all that hard work?

options.A: Perimetrium
options.B: Endometrium
options.C: Myometrium
options.D: Cervical os

explanation: Spot on! The myometrium is made of tough, powerful smooth muscle designed to push the baby safely into the world.

question: Who are the key local partners working alongside community nurses during an emergency?

options.A: Community health extension workers, midwives, and local transport providers
options.B: International pharmaceutical manufacturers and corporate executives
options.C: Hospital accountants and administrative billing officers
options.D: Architects and building construction contractors

explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! Community nurses rely closely on CHEWs, midwives, and local drivers to handle crises smoothly.

question: When a hospital is planning space for future needs, what data is most important to look at?

options.A: The architectural styles used in other commercial buildings
options.B: Patient admission trends and local population changes
options.C: The cost of office furniture and administrative supplies
options.D: The personal preferences of the hospital board members

explanation: To plan for tomorrow, planners must check how many patients have been coming in and how the local community is growing. It is all about meeting real community needs!

question: What kind of air pressure is kept in the CSSD washing and decontamination room?

options.A: Neutral air pressure
options.B: Negative air pressure
options.C: Positive air pressure
options.D: Variable air pressure

explanation: Think of negative pressure like a vacuum that sucks air in. It pulls air into the room instead of blowing it out, keeping dirty germs trapped safely inside the washing area.

question: Why do sudden increases in food prices hurt low-income households much harder than wealthy households?

options.A: Low-income families consume fewer total calories than wealthy individuals
options.B: Low-income households spend a much larger share of their total income on basic food items
options.C: Wealthy households are legally prohibited from buying discounted grocery items
options.D: Grocery stores charge high-income earners extra taxes on all purchases

explanation: When food takes up most of a family's budget, even a slight price hike leaves them with little room to adjust. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h7)

question: What is the main job of the posterior pituitary gland?

options.A: It breaks down worn-out hormones in the bloodstream
options.B: It stores and releases hormones produced by the hypothalamus
options.C: It manufactures tropic hormones for the adrenal glands
options.D: It controls blood calcium levels using direct neural input

explanation: The posterior pituitary acts like a warehouse—it doesn't make hormones itself, but safely stores and releases them when needed.

question: When is the best time for a nurse to educate an expectant mum about potential prenatal vitamin side effects?

options.A: At the child's one-year checkup
options.B: Only after a fecal impaction occurs
options.C: Early in the prenatal care schedule
options.D: During the postpartum hospital discharge

explanation: Brilliant! Teaching mums early means they can adjust their diet and water intake before vitamin side effects become a painful problem.

question: A 13-year-old girl comes to the clinic showing frequent injuries and signs of poor nutrition. What should be an early suspicion for the nurse?

options.A: Potential abuse and vulnerability linked to an early forced union
options.B: Normal developmental changes associated with puberty
options.C: A rare genetic metabolic disorder affecting bone strength
options.D: Intentional self-harm due to school academic pressure

explanation: Repeated injuries and malnutrition in a very young girl often point to domestic mistreatment and early marriage.

question: Why is continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) often chosen over standard hemodialysis for critically ill patients?

options.A: It can be performed easily without any specialized equipment
options.B: It does not require any form of vascular access in the body
options.C: It completely cures chronic kidney disease within a few days
options.D: It removes fluids and toxins much more slowly and gently

explanation: CRRT filters blood continuously over 24 hours, making it much safer for hemodynamically unstable patients in the ICU. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T6#GNS213_U4_T6_h7)

question: What is the main job of oxytocin during breastfeeding?

options.A: Triggering the milk ejection reflex
options.B: Preventing breast infections
options.C: Stopping milk production
options.D: Stimulating breast tissue growth

explanation: Oxytocin helps let the milk flow out (the milk ejection reflex) when the baby nurses. It's the hormone of love and bonding too!

question: In nursing, what does the term 'medication adherence' actually mean?

options.A: The speed at which a drug dissolves in the gastrointestinal tract
options.B: The extent to which a patient takes their medication as agreed with providers
options.C: The chemical binding force holding tablet ingredients together
options.D: The physical strength of the plastic bottle cap protecting the pills

explanation: Adherence is just a teamwork word for whether the patient is taking their drugs the way you both agreed on.

question: How does community critical care connect to wider public health goals?

options.A: By tracking disease outbreaks, educating the public, and promoting early recognition of danger signs
options.B: By replacing all national public health vaccination programs
options.C: By focusing exclusively on treating isolated patients inside locked clinic rooms
options.D: By restricting health education to urban teaching hospitals only

explanation: Community nursing goes beyond the clinic doors by keeping an eye out for outbreaks and teaching families how to spot danger early.

question: Which vitamin is synthesized in the skin when exposed to sunlight?

options.A: Vitamin C
options.B: Vitamin D
options.C: Vitamin K
options.D: Vitamin A

explanation: Ultraviolet light helps convert cholesterol compounds in the skin into active vitamin D precursors necessary for bone health. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why might the standard 0-to-10 numeric pain scale be tricky to use for an adult with severe dementia?

options.A: Numeric scales only work for surgical wounds
options.B: Patients with dementia lose the ability to speak at all
options.C: They will always just say ten no matter what
options.D: They may struggle to connect a number to how they feel

explanation: Well reasoned! Numbers are abstract concepts. For patients with cognitive changes, we often need to rely on facial expression charts or physical behavior cues instead.

question: What is required before giving any medication authorized by a standing order?

options.A: Asking the patient to pay double the standard consultation fee
options.B: Waiting for a written countersignature from the state governor
options.C: Storing the medication in direct sunlight for at least one hour
options.D: Verifying the safety rights such as right patient, drug, and dose

explanation: Standard drug administration safety rules must always be followed, regardless of whether a drug is given via a standing order or a direct prescription. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T6#GNS124_U6_T6_h6)

question: Why do we tell patients to elevate a sprained ankle above the level of the heart?

options.A: It increases arterial blood flow to speed up ligament fiber regeneration
options.B: Elevation prevents the development of systemic blood clots in the leg
options.C: Gravity helps drain excess fluid and reduce swelling at the injury site
options.D: It relaxes the calf muscles so the bone fracture can heal properly

explanation: Elevation uses gravity to pull extra fluid away from the injured area, helping to bring down that painful swelling.

question: What is an ovarian cyst?

options.A: A solid tumor growing inside the uterus
options.B: A complete blockage of the vaginal canal
options.C: An infection of the fallopian tubes
options.D: A fluid-filled sac on or inside an ovary

explanation: Ovarian cysts are pockets or sacs filled with fluid that develop on or inside the ovarian tissue. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T32#GNS216_U5_T32_h1)

question: Why is watching a patient actually do a household task better than just asking if they can do it?

options.A: Patients often lie to nurses to avoid being sent away to a hospital.
options.B: Verbal reports may not match the patient's actual physical capability.
options.C: Patients forget the names of the tools they use for cooking and cleaning.
options.D: Direct observation is a mandatory legal requirement in all provinces.

explanation: Spot on! People often overestimate what they can do or try to hide their struggles, so watching them yourself gives you the true picture.

question: Why is using misoprostol by itself very common in areas with limited healthcare resources?

options.A: It is widely available, affordable, and effective on its own
options.B: It completely prevents all normal cramping and heavy bleeding
options.C: It removes the need for any follow-up care
options.D: It works twice as fast as other drug combos

explanation: Because mifepristone is hard to get in many places, using misoprostol alone provides a practical and accessible option for safe care. Great job!

question: A patient is drowsy and can only be woken up when you apply strong, painful physical stimuli. What is this level of consciousness called?

options.A: Lethargy
options.B: Obtundation
options.C: Confusion
options.D: Stupor

explanation: When a patient is in a stupor, they are deeply asleep or unresponsive, and it takes strong physical prodding to get them to react. You've got this!

question: Where should used injection needles and sharp blades be discarded?

options.A: Puncture-proof sharps containers
options.B: Red infectious linen laundry bags
options.C: Open cardboard boxes near sinks
options.D: Standard black plastic waste bins

explanation: Sharps must go directly into rigid, puncture-resistant containers to prevent accidental needle pricks. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h6)

question: A community health nurse visits a nursery and notices toys scattered on the floor that easily fit inside an infant's mouth. What immediate safety hazard does this present?

options.A: Risk of chemical poisoning from plastic
options.B: Risk of electrical shock from the floor
options.C: Risk of choking and airway obstruction
options.D: Risk of severe ultraviolet radiation damage

explanation: Small objects that fit into an infant's mouth pose an immediate choking hazard and must be removed from play areas. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h3)

question: Which communication trick helps a nurse truly understand what a patient normally eats?

options.A: Assuming all patients eat the same traditional hospital diet
options.B: Handing out a pamphlet and asking if they can read
options.C: Reading a strict list of forbidden foods and waiting for agreement
options.D: Asking open-ended questions about what foods the patient eats at home

explanation: Open-ended questions like 'Tell me what you usually eat in a day' invite honest chats and help you give advice that fits their real life.

question: What is the name of the condition marked by lung inflammation and high white blood cells (eosinophils) when roundworm larvae travel through the lungs?

options.A: Nephrotic syndrome
options.B: Compartment syndrome
options.C: Cushing's syndrome
options.D: Loeffler's syndrome

explanation: Loeffler's syndrome happens when migrating parasite larvae cause temporary respiratory symptoms and changes in the lungs.

question: What type of strong connective tissue attaches skeletal muscles directly to bones?

options.A: Tendon
options.B: Synovium
options.C: Ligament
options.D: Cartilage

explanation: You got it! Tendons connect muscle to bone (remember: 'T'endon = 'T'ies muscle to bone), while ligaments connect bone to bone.

question: When calculating the incidence of a disease, what goes on top (the numerator)?

options.A: The number of new cases developed during a period
options.B: The entire population living in the community
options.C: The number of patients who recovered completely
options.D: The total number of people who died from old age

explanation: Great job! The numerator in an incidence formula always focuses strictly on the newly diagnosed cases.

question: What is the best home-care advice for a patient's small wound sites after laparoscopy?

options.A: Scrub the incisions vigorously with a rough sponge
options.B: Apply heavy grease daily to speed up healing
options.C: Keep the puncture sites clean and dry
options.D: Remove the surgical steri-strips immediately

explanation: Correct! Keeping tiny cut sites clean and dry keeps germs away and lets them heal nicely without any trouble.

question: Which vitamin helps the body absorb plant-based iron much better?

options.A: Vitamin E
options.B: Vitamin D
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Vitamin K

explanation: Taking vitamin C alongside plant-based iron sources significantly improves how well the gut absorbs the mineral. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T15#GNS311_U2_T15_h2)

question: How do long, slow government approval processes harm a revolving drug fund?

options.A: It forces patients to buy better quality drugs from abroad
options.B: It gives the pharmacy staff extra time to clean the shelves
options.C: It causes pharmaceutical companies to lower their wholesale prices
options.D: Inflation reduces the real purchasing power of the cash while waiting

explanation: Spot on! When approvals drag on for months, prices go up, meaning your saved cash can suddenly buy way fewer drugs than before.

question: During peritoneal dialysis, what part of the patient's body acts as the natural filtering membrane?

options.A: The peritoneal membrane inside the abdominal cavity
options.B: The inner lining of the urinary bladder walls
options.C: The basement membrane of the remaining renal tubules
options.D: The semipermeable filter inside the hemodialysis machine

explanation: Peritoneal dialysis is clever! It uses the patient's own rich network of blood vessels inside the abdominal lining (the peritoneum) to filter out waste and extra water.

question: How can you best help a patient with a tracheostomy tube who temporarily cannot speak?

options.A: Temporarily remove parts of the tube
options.B: Provide writing pads or communication boards
options.C: Tell them to whisper to keep their voice strong
options.D: Ask only yes-or-no questions for head nods

explanation: Spot on! Alternative tools like writing boards let patients express themselves clearly without straining or irritating their airway.

question: Which of these body areas is a classic, go-to site for giving a subcutaneous injection?

options.A: The sole of the foot
options.B: The abdomen
options.C: The center of the chest
options.D: The palm of the hand

explanation: That's right! The abdomen is a favorite spot for everyday injections like insulin and heparin because it has a nice, accessible layer of fat.

question: What is the main laboratory test used to detect chlamydia and gonorrhea from a swab or urine sample?

options.A: Nucleic Acid Amplification Tests
options.B: Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay
options.C: Stool occult blood analysis
options.D: Complete blood count with differential

explanation: NAATs are the gold standard! They accurately copy and spot tiny amounts of the germ's genetic material.

question: Why is it so important to plan care goals together with the client and their family?

options.A: To shift all legal responsibility for treatment onto the family
options.B: Because care happens in their personal space and must fit their daily reality
options.C: Because hospital rules legally apply to all home settings
options.D: To make sure the nurse does not have to do any heavy lifting

explanation: You got it! As nurses visiting someone's home, our plan has to make sense for their everyday life, or it simply won't work.

question: What is the main reason governments place heavy taxes on tobacco and sugary drinks?

options.A: To completely ban all agricultural farming activities in rural farming communities
options.B: To fund the construction of large international airports in every state capital
options.C: To make healthcare workers richer through direct salary commission bonuses
options.D: To discourage consumption and lower the population's risk of developing NCDs

explanation: Spot on! When unhealthy items become more expensive, people tend to buy less of them, which helps lower community rates of lifestyle diseases.

question: Which nursing action is strictly forbidden during the initial assessment of a patient bleeding in late pregnancy?

options.A: Checking the maternal blood pressure
options.B: Palpating the abdominal wall gently
options.C: Performing a digital vaginal examination
options.D: Monitoring the fetal heart rate

explanation: Never do a digital vaginal exam when late pregnancy bleeding is unexplained, because it can provoke severe hemorrhage if placenta praevia is present! Safety first!

question: How does aldosterone help raise blood pressure once it is released during the RAAS cascade?

options.A: It forces the heart to beat much faster
options.B: It causes the kidneys to retain sodium and water
options.C: It relaxes blood vessels throughout the body
options.D: It triggers the thirst center in the brain

explanation: Aldosterone signals the renal tubules to reabsorb sodium, pulling water along with it to increase blood volume and pressure. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T8#GNS121_U2_T8_h3)

question: How do dendrites differ in function from axons?

options.A: Dendrites are found only in the brain, while axons are in the spinal cord
options.B: Dendrites carry signals toward the cell body, while axons carry them away
options.C: Dendrites produce myelin, while axons produce neurotransmitters
options.D: Dendrites control voluntary movement, while axons control involuntary actions

explanation: Dendrites act as receiving antennas, whereas axons transmit the nerve impulse outward to other cells. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T1#GNS222_U3_T1_h5)

question: In a community health project, money, medical supplies, and trained personnel are known as what?

options.A: Inputs
options.B: Outcomes
options.C: Outputs
options.D: Impacts

explanation: Inputs are the raw resources, funds, and staff you put *in* to get the project started. You've got this!

question: What is the main goal of food safety in primary health care?

options.A: Disease prevention and health promotion
options.B: Regulating international food trade
options.C: Managing surgical theatre sterility
options.D: Treating advanced chronic illnesses

explanation: You've got this! Food safety at the primary health care level is all about stopping foodborne illnesses before they start and helping our communities stay healthy and strong.

question: How do the intrinsic and extrinsic pathways work together in the body?

options.A: They both activate a series of clotting factors that lead into the common pathway
options.B: They regulate the exact volume of blood pumped by the heart
options.C: They prevent platelets from sticking to healthy blood vessels
options.D: They work in opposite directions to dissolve unwanted blood clots

explanation: Both pathways act as separate starting points that eventually feed into the same shared sequence to produce a solid clot. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h3)

question: What should a nurse do when a patient refuses to take a prescribed oral medication?

options.A: Document the refusal and notify the prescribing doctor
options.B: Hide the crushed pill inside sweet food without telling them
options.C: Force the medication gently by holding the patient's jaw
options.D: Leave the pill on the bedside table for them to take later

explanation: Competent patients have the right to refuse treatment, and the care team must be informed to adjust the plan. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T1#GNS122_U1_T1_h5)

question: How do sutures and fontanelles help make vaginal delivery safe for the baby?

options.A: They absorb all the physical shock so the baby feels no pressure
options.B: They prevent the brain from swelling when the mother pushes
options.C: They produce lubricating fluid that helps the head slide out smoothly
options.D: They allow the skull to reduce its size by letting bones move closer together

explanation: Exactly! The gaps give the skull bones room to shift and overlap, shrinking the head's diameter so it can pass through the pelvis safely.

question: A patient comes in after a clandestine abortion with a high fever, smelly vaginal discharge, and lower tummy pain. What is the most likely problem?

options.A: Normal postpartum involution
options.B: Pelvic inflammatory sepsis
options.C: Uncomplicated uterine atony
options.D: Primary ovarian hyperstimulation

explanation: Fever plus foul-smelling discharge is a red flag for infection. Unsterile instruments easily introduce bacteria right into the uterus, leading quickly to pelvic sepsis. Great clinical spotting!

question: Which specialized structure inside the ventricles makes cerebrospinal fluid?

options.A: Dural venous sinus
options.B: Arachnoid granulations
options.C: Choroid plexus
options.D: Cerebral cortex

explanation: Brilliant! The choroid plexus is like a tiny, hardworking sponge network inside the ventricles that constantly produces fresh cerebrospinal fluid.

question: How should past studies be presented in a good literature review?

options.A: A random list of book titles found in the library
options.B: Unchecked rumors heard around the hospital ward
options.C: Personal diary entries written by the researcher
options.D: A critical analysis and grouping of past studies by themes

explanation: Instead of just listing past papers one by one, you group them by themes and discuss what they mean together.

question: A patient is admitted with active pulmonary tuberculosis. Which precaution should you put in place?

options.A: Standard precautions only
options.B: Airborne precautions
options.C: Contact precautions
options.D: Vector control measures

explanation: Because TB germs float around in tiny droplets in the air when the patient coughs, we need special ventilation and masks to keep everyone safe!

question: How does repeated simulation practice affect a nursing student's clinical performance?

options.A: It makes them overly confident and careless with hospital procedures
options.B: It has no noticeable effect on how they care for real patients
options.C: It builds confidence and reduces the learning curve on real patients
options.D: It increases anxiety and makes them freeze up during real emergencies

explanation: Having practiced a procedure or crisis response in the lab helps students perform calmly and competently at the bedside. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T8#GNS212_U4_T8_h6)

question: Which tissue type burns more calories at rest?

options.A: Bone matrix
options.B: Blood plasma
options.C: Muscle tissue
options.D: Adipose tissue

explanation: Muscle is metabolically active tissue that burns more energy at rest than fat (adipose) tissue. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T008#GNS227_U4_T008_h5)

question: What is Manual Vacuum Aspiration (MVA) mainly used for in post-abortion care?

options.A: Safely emptying the uterus of retained products of conception
options.B: Inducing long-term hormonal contraception to prevent pregnancy
options.C: Suturing cervical lacerations caused by traumatic instrumentation
options.D: Delivering strong intravenous antibiotics to treat pelvic sepsis

explanation: Exactly! MVA uses a safe, specialized syringe system to quickly clear out the uterine cavity during early pregnancy complications.

question: What is the normal, healthy pH range for human blood?
explanation: Memorize this tiny golden window! Staying between 7.35 and 7.45 keeps all our body enzymes working happily.

question: Why might you need to watch a patient for whole-body (systemic) effects after applying a topical cream or patch?

options.A: Skin application always causes widespread allergic reactions.
options.B: Topical drugs change the local skin temperature, affecting blood pressure.
options.C: Some topical agents are designed to cross the skin barrier and enter the bloodstream.
options.D: All topical drugs automatically travel to the liver first before working.

explanation: Spot on! While many stay local, formulations like transdermal patches are specially made to pass through the skin into the bloodstream to heal the whole body.

question: Which hardworking hormone tells the kidneys to hold onto sodium and water while letting go of potassium?

options.A: Thyroxine
options.B: Aldosterone
options.C: Estrogen
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Aldosterone is your kidney's best friend for saving water and sodium when your body needs to boost its volume. You're crushing it!

question: What is a major social reason families continue to practice FGM?

options.A: Compliance with international health mandates
options.B: A direct recommendation by the national medical association
options.C: The prevention of childhood infectious diseases
options.D: Fear of social exclusion and unmarriageability

explanation: Sadly, many families do it because they fear their daughters will be rejected by the community or struggle to find husbands. Understanding this helps you treat patients with empathy.

question: Which blood pressure range is classified as Stage 1 Hypertension?

options.A: 140 or higher systolic or 90 or higher diastolic
options.B: Below 120 systolic and below 80 diastolic
options.C: 130-139 systolic or 80-89 diastolic
options.D: 120-129 systolic and under 80 diastolic

explanation: Stage 1 hypertension starts when the top number is 130-139 or the bottom number is 80-89. Good numbers to keep in mind for your clinicals!

question: Why does severe anemia make mothers so vulnerable to dying from postpartum hemorrhage?

options.A: It prevents the placenta from forming correctly in the first trimester
options.B: It directly causes high blood pressure and seizures
options.C: It leaves women with very little physiological reserve to survive normal blood loss during delivery
options.D: It stops uterine contractions during the second stage of labor

explanation: Makes total sense when you think about it: if a woman is already low on blood (anemic), even normal blood loss during delivery can quickly throw her into shock. Always push for iron supplements during ANC!

question: What is the main medical treatment for long-term (chronic) hypoparathyroidism?

options.A: Intravenous calcitonin injections given twice daily
options.B: High-dose potassium replacement therapy
options.C: Oral calcium supplements combined with active vitamin D
options.D: Daily doses of oral bisphosphonates to protect bones

explanation: Since the body isn't making enough PTH on its own, patients take oral calcium and active vitamin D as a tag-team effort to keep blood calcium stable.

question: What is the main job of the tiny bones (ossicles) inside your middle ear?

options.A: To amplify and transmit sound vibrations to the cochlea
options.B: To filter and warm incoming air before it reaches the lungs
options.C: To produce endolymph and maintain fluid pressure in the inner ear
options.D: To equalize air pressure between the ear canal and the throat

explanation: The malleus, incus, and stapes work together like a tiny lever system to boost the strength of sound waves as they travel from the air into the fluid-filled inner ear. Brilliant work!

question: What is a major reason for high maternal mortality rates in many rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: Limited access to skilled birth attendants and emergency obstetric care
options.B: Universal free access to advanced reproductive technology
options.C: Mandatory hospital deliveries for all pregnant women
options.D: An overabundance of licensed gynecologists in primary health centers

explanation: When clinics are far away and transport is hard to find, delays in getting emergency care during childbirth sadly put many mothers at high risk.

question: Which of the following is NOT a major challenge faced by public health nurses in many parts of Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive availability of ultra-modern robotic surgery equipment
options.B: Navigating cultural barriers and vaccine hesitancy in communities
options.C: Funding shortages affecting routine immunization supplies
options.D: Infrastructural deficits and poor road networks in remote areas

explanation: Robotic surgery equipment is found in advanced tertiary centers, not primary health care settings, making it an incorrect challenge for public health nurses. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h7)

question: Which major electrolyte hangs out mostly INSIDE our body cells (the intracellular fluid)?

options.A: Chloride
options.B: Sodium
options.C: Calcium
options.D: Potassium

explanation: You've got this! Think of potassium as the main star inside the cells, while sodium rules the outside world. Keep up the great work!

question: Why are daily reviews of invasive lines and breathing tubes an important part of complication prevention?

options.A: Hospital insurance policies require equipment to be changed daily.
options.B: It gives the nursing staff less paperwork to complete at shift change.
options.C: Removing them as soon as they are no longer needed lowers infection risks.
options.D: Patients prefer to have new lines poked into them every morning.

explanation: Every day a tube or line stays inside the body gives bacteria more time to enter and cause a severe infection. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T4#GNS321_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is a major ethical dilemma an occupational health nurse frequently faces?

options.A: Deciding whether to do surgery without a doctor
options.B: Balancing loyalty to the employer with the duty to protect worker health and privacy
options.C: Choosing between clinical nursing and selling products
options.D: Reporting fellow nurses to criminal courts for minor errors

explanation: Spot on! Because the company pays your salary but nursing ethics demand patient privacy, it can be a tough tightrope to walk.

question: Why is the role of the bedside nurse so vital to national disease surveillance?

options.A: Nurses write all national health policies approved in parliament
options.B: Nurses manufacture all laboratory testing kits used in the country
options.C: Nurses personally fund international rapid response medical teams
options.D: Nurses often spot unusual clinical cases first and trigger early alerts

explanation: Because nurses care directly for patients, they are usually the first to notice unusual symptoms or clustering that signals an emerging outbreak. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h9)

question: Think of a research design as a step-by-step plan. What is its main job in nursing?

options.A: To secure ethical approval from the hospital board
options.B: To calculate the exact financial cost of a hospital study
options.C: To write the final reference list for a journal article
options.D: To act as a blueprint for answering a clinical question

explanation: Spot on! Just like building a house needs a good plan, a research design is your overall framework that guides how you answer a specific clinical question.

question: What is the primary indicator that the needle has successfully entered the lumen of the vein during insertion?

options.A: The surrounding skin turns pale and cold to the touch.
options.B: The patient reports a warm, soothing sensation in the hand.
options.C: A flashback of blood appears in the catheter hub chamber.
options.D: The tourniquet drops off the patient's arm automatically.

explanation: Blood entering the flash chamber confirms that the needle tip is inside the blood vessel before advancing the plastic cannula. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T16#GNS122_U1_T16_h5)

question: What does a black, tarry stool sample usually tell you about your patient?

options.A: Bleeding in the upper gastrointestinal tract
options.B: Bleeding in the lower rectum or anus
options.C: Severe dehydration and low fluid intake
options.D: A high intake of green leafy vegetables

explanation: As blood travels all the way from the stomach through the gut, digestive juices break it down, turning it dark and tarry by the time it comes out.

question: What is the main purpose of secondary prevention, like routine screenings?

options.A: Stopping environmental toxins from entering the local community
options.B: Preventing healthy individuals from ever encountering risk factors
options.C: Restoring full physical strength after cancer treatment finishes
options.D: Detecting disease early when it is easiest and most successful to treat

explanation: Secondary prevention is all about catching things early through screening so you can tackle them before they grow into a bigger problem.

question: Which situation means a child needs intravenous (IV) fluids right away?

options.A: Low-grade fever lasting less than an hour
options.B: A slight decrease in daily appetite
options.C: Mild loose stool passed twice in one day
options.D: Severe dehydration with signs of shock

explanation: When shock and severe dehydration set in, drinking isn't enough anymore. IV fluids are urgently needed to restore blood pressure and save the day.

question: Why is spotting a specific 'toxidrome' (group of symptoms) so helpful in emergency care?

options.A: It proves legal liability for workplace safety violations
options.B: It stops the chemical from absorbing through unbroken skin
options.C: It guides rapid clinical management before lab tests confirm the toxin
options.D: It eliminates the need to decontaminate the patient's clothing

explanation: Lab tests take time! Spotting a familiar pattern of symptoms lets you start life-saving antidotes and care right away.

question: Why do we treat evaluation as an ongoing process rather than a one-time thing?

options.A: Patients prefer being tested multiple times a day
options.B: Hospital accreditation bodies require it to happen every hour
options.C: It prevents nurses from having to document patient care
options.D: It allows nurses to make continuous adjustments to care plans and learning strategies

explanation: Checking in continuously lets you catch issues early and tweak your care plan in real-time. It's all about helping your patient get better faster!

question: What happens to the arterioles in your muscles when you start heavy exercise?

options.A: They collapse completely to stop bleeding
options.B: They harden permanently to boost pressure
options.C: They dilate to let more blood through
options.D: They constrict to block fast blood flow

explanation: Working muscles need more oxygen, so local arterioles relax and open wide to increase blood supply. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h3)

question: As a community health nurse, what is your most important role in tackling the health effects of son preference?

options.A: Reporting every family without a male child directly to the local police
options.B: Forcing husbands to attend mandatory gender sensitivity tribunal sessions
options.C: Providing family planning counseling and educating communities on maternal health risks
options.D: Providing financial grants to families that successfully birth a female child

explanation: Education and family planning are our best tools to protect mothers from the dangers of repeated, unplanned pregnancies.

question: What does an anterior body landmark refer to?

options.A: A structure located on the front of the body
options.B: A structure located on the back of the body
options.C: A bony prominence found only on the skull
options.D: A deep internal organ with no surface visibility

explanation: Anterior landmarks are situated on the front or ventral surface of the human body. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is the most common trigger for a breakthrough seizure in someone with epilepsy?

options.A: Drinking cold water
options.B: Eating too much sugar
options.C: Walking outside in bright sunlight
options.D: Missing prescribed medication doses

explanation: Consistency is key! Skipping meds lets the drug levels drop in the blood, making a seizure much more likely to happen. Remind your patients how important their schedule is.

question: When should standard precautions be used in clinical practice?

options.A: Only when blood or body fluid is visibly staining the bedsheets
options.B: To every patient, regardless of their diagnosis or infection status
options.C: Strictly during surgical procedures in the main operating theatre
options.D: Only when caring for patients with known infectious diseases

explanation: Treat every patient as potentially infectious. Standard precautions keep you and everyone around you safe from hidden germs.

question: What are you comparing when you perform a 'gap analysis' in community health?

options.A: The age of children versus the age of their grandparents
options.B: Current health status against desired health standards
options.C: The salary of nurses versus doctors in the clinic
options.D: Total population size against total land area in kilometers

explanation: A gap analysis simply looks at the gap between where the community's health is right now and the healthy standard we want them to achieve.

question: What should you do if a patient cannot speak because they have an endotracheal breathing tube in their throat?

options.A: Score the patient with a verbal score of 1 for total silence
options.B: Give the patient a verbal score of 5 assuming they are normal
options.C: Document the verbal score as untestable and note the breathing tube
options.D: Leave the verbal score section completely blank on the chart

explanation: Never guess! When a physical barrier like a breathing tube stops you from testing, clearly document why you couldn't check it so other nurses understand.

question: An antibiotic costs 500 Naira to land in the pharmacy, and hospital policy adds a 20 percent mark-up. What is the retail price?

options.A: 520 Naira
options.B: 550 Naira
options.C: 600 Naira
options.D: 700 Naira

explanation: Let's do the quick math: 20 percent of 500 Naira is 100 Naira. Add that mark-up to the original 500 Naira cost, and you get a final retail price of 600 Naira. Easy peasy!

question: Which of these is NOT something a community health nurse should do when promoting family planning?

options.A: Ensuring client confidentiality during health consultations
options.B: Dispelling common myths regarding modern contraceptive safety
options.C: Providing accurate counseling on various birth control options
options.D: Forcing community members to adopt specific contraceptive devices

explanation: You got it! Family planning must always be a personal choice. Forcing anyone goes against nursing ethics and human rights.

question: Why does sudden, heavy bleeding (acute blood loss) often cause tachycardia?

options.A: Low blood pressure completely shuts off parasympathetic signals
options.B: Red blood cells speed up electrical conduction when counts drop
options.C: The body compensates for low blood volume by making the heart pump faster
options.D: Bleeding directly irritates the SA node with excess iron

explanation: When blood volume drops, your clever body tries to keep blood flowing to vital organs by speeding up the heart to make up for the lower volume.

question: What happens if you use a single-dose medication vial for more than one patient?

options.A: It changes the chemical concentration of the prescribed drug
options.B: It transfers invisible pathogens between patients via contaminated equipment
options.C: It causes the remaining medicine to expire instantly
options.D: It increases the physical pain experienced during injection

explanation: Single-dose vials don't have preservatives. Reusing them lets germs multiply and spread infections to the next patient. Always use one vial per patient!

question: Which test gives the best quick check of oxygen, carbon dioxide, and acid-base balance in a crashing patient?

options.A: Full blood count
options.B: Urinalysis
options.C: Stool microscopy
options.D: Arterial blood gases

explanation: ABGs give you the full picture of how well the lungs are oxygenating the blood and clearing out waste gases. You'll master this in clinicals!

question: Why is it best to look up medications by their generic name in the formulary?

options.A: It prevents confusion because one drug can have many different brand names
options.B: It stops patients from experiencing any side effects
options.C: It ensures the medication is always available free of charge
options.D: It proves that the drug was manufactured locally in Nigeria

explanation: A single drug can have dozens of brand names, but the generic name is always the same everywhere in the world!

question: Which of these is a classic sign that a patient might have hypothyroidism?

options.A: Rapid and unintended weight loss
options.B: High resting heart rate or tachycardia
options.C: Excessive nervousness and tremors
options.D: Intolerance to cold temperatures

explanation: A sluggish thyroid slows down the body's metabolism and heat production. Because of this, hypothyroid patients often feel freezing cold even when everyone else is comfortable.

question: Which of these is a common cause of an inaccurate glucometer reading?

options.A: Using too little blood on the test strip
options.B: Pricking the side of the finger
options.C: Wiping the outside of the meter clean
options.D: Checking blood sugar before breakfast

explanation: The strip needs enough blood to fill the reaction zone. If the sample is too small, the meter might give an error or a false reading.

question: How can a nurse best check a baby's skin for a yellow tint during a physical exam?

options.A: Gently pressing the skin over a bony prominence to blanch it
options.B: Pinching a fold of skin on the baby's arm to test elasticity
options.C: Observing the baby inside a dark room using a standard flashlight
options.D: Shining a blue phototherapy light directly onto the infant's abdomen

explanation: Pressing gently over a bone clears the surface blood for a second, making the underlying yellow bilirubin tint much easier to spot. Simple and effective bedside nursing!

question: How does viewing the family as the unit of care change your daily practice as a nurse?

options.A: You avoid giving individual medications to teenagers
options.B: You focus exclusively on genetic disorders during visits
options.C: You spend most of your shift counseling only the head of the household
options.D: You look beyond the sick patient to consider their home support and environment

explanation: Spotting home support and barriers helps you understand why a treatment plan might succeed or struggle at home.

question: What is the main reason nurses use hypothesis testing in research?

options.A: To prove that personal clinical opinions are always correct
options.B: To increase the financial cost of operating a hospital ward
options.C: To evaluate if observed data differences are real or due to chance
options.D: To eliminate the need for collecting patient outcome data

explanation: Great job thinking like a researcher! Hypothesis testing simply uses math to check if what we see in a study is a true effect or just random luck. You've got this!

question: A patient with a chest stab wound suddenly loses their pulse and shows PEA (pulseless electrical activity) on the monitor. What is the best immediate action?

options.A: Wait for a formal chest X-ray to confirm the cardiac arrest
options.B: Place the patient in a flat, prone position to rest the back
options.C: Administer oral blood pressure medications through a feeding tube
options.D: Prepare equipment for emergency thoracotomy and active resuscitation

explanation: Traumatic arrest with PEA is a critical emergency. It often needs immediate teamwork, resuscitation, and sometimes opening the chest in the trauma bay to save the patient's life.

question: Eighteen months after losing her husband, a widow still cannot leave her house, eat well, or talk about him without panicking. What kind of grief is she experiencing?

options.A: Anticipatory grief
options.B: Complicated grief
options.C: Delayed grief
options.D: Normal grief

explanation: When grief stays extreme and stops someone from living their normal life long after a loss, we call it complicated grief.

question: What is the main danger of leaving a collected lab specimen sitting at room temperature for too long?

options.A: Bacteria can multiply and cells can break down, giving false results
options.B: The label on the container will automatically fade and fall off
options.C: The specimen container will become legally invalid for testing
options.D: Hospital management will issue a fine for delayed paperwork

explanation: Time matters! Leaving samples sitting around lets bacteria multiply or cells decay, which ruins the accuracy of the test.

question: You walk into a stuffy ward, fling the windows open to let in fresh air, and tidy up a messy bedside. Whose classic nursing theory are you putting into action?

options.A: Hildegard Peplau
options.B: Florence Nightingale
options.C: Dorothea Orem
options.D: Virginia Henderson

explanation: Brilliant! Opening windows and clearing away dirt are the ultimate trademark moves of Nightingale's Environmental Theory.

question: What critical instruction must a nurse give a patient before they apply a fresh transdermal patch?

options.A: Apply the new patch directly on top of the old patch
options.B: Wash the old patch with soap and leave it in place
options.C: Remove the old patch before putting on the new one
options.D: Cut the new patch in half to double the lifespan

explanation: Leaving an old patch on while applying a new one causes dangerous drug overdosing because medication continues to absorb from both patches. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h8)

question: Why do hydatid cysts often go unnoticed for a long time after infection?

options.A: They dissolve quickly inside the bloodstream
options.B: They grow very slowly over months or years
options.C: They immediately trigger severe immune rejection
options.D: They only affect areas with no nerve supply

explanation: Because these cysts grow so slowly, they stay quiet and hidden for a long time before crowding nearby organs.

question: How do you know if a data collection tool (like a questionnaire) is truly valid?

options.A: It accurately measures what it is intended to measure
options.B: It has been approved by the hospital accountant
options.C: It is extremely cheap to print and distribute
options.D: It takes less than two minutes for patients to finish

explanation: Validity just means your tool does the job it's supposed to do—it's actually testing the specific variable you care about.

question: You receive a transcribed drug order with blurry handwriting and an old shorthand symbol. What is your best next step?

options.A: Ask another student nurse to guess what the symbol might mean
options.B: Wait until the patient's shift ends and let the next nurse handle it
options.C: Ask the prescribing clinician to clarify the order before administration
options.D: Administer the lowest possible dose listed in the pharmacy manual

explanation: You got it! When handwriting is blurry or abbreviations are confusing, always go straight to the prescriber to get clear instructions. Patient safety is always number one.

question: How do medications like penicillin actually destroy bacterial cells?

options.A: By mimicking vital human hormones
options.B: By breaking down the protective cell wall
options.C: By increasing the acidity of the blood
options.D: By blocking the replication of human DNA

explanation: Think of the cell wall as the bacteria's armor. Penicillin weakens this wall so it bursts open and dies!

question: During labor, a first-time mother with a history of Type III FGM is at the highest risk for which complication?

options.A: Complete absence of uterine contractions
options.B: Rapid precipitous delivery within ten minutes
options.C: Obstructed labor due to rigid scar tissue
options.D: Immediate postpartum hemorrhage from the placenta

explanation: The tough scar tissue from infibulation makes it hard for the birth canal to stretch naturally, frequently leading to obstructed labor.

question: Which type of drug works mainly by swelling up with water to stretch the intestinal wall and trigger movement?

options.A: Bulk-forming agents
options.B: Stimulant purgatives
options.C: Stool softeners
options.D: Saline cathartics

explanation: You got it! Bulk-forming agents absorb fluid and expand, increasing stool size so the bowel naturally contracts to push it out.

question: What usually happens when a healthcare facility does not have a clear organisational structure?

options.A: Better coordination among different hospital departments
options.B: Instant improvement in employee satisfaction scores
options.C: Confusion over job roles and delayed decisions
options.D: A sharp increase in the recruitment of new nurses

explanation: Without clear reporting lines, staff get confused about whose job is whose, and simple decisions take forever. A clear structure prevents this headache!

question: Why should nurses advise patients NEVER to put butter or toothpaste on a fresh burn?

options.A: They cause the top layer of skin to fall off immediately
options.B: These substances trap heat inside the tissue and can introduce bacteria
options.C: They react chemically with sweat to produce dangerous acid
options.D: They neutralize cool tap water and make the wound freeze faster

explanation: Spot on! Kitchen remedies like butter act like a blanket, keeping the heat trapped inside and inviting germs that cause infections.

question: Which common practice puts people at high risk for Lassa fever by letting rodents touch food?

options.A: Keeping domestic cats inside the main living areas at night
options.B: Drying food crops out in the open on mats or bare ground
options.C: Storing clean drinking water inside tightly sealed plastic containers
options.D: Washing cooking utensils immediately after every family meal

explanation: Spot on! Leaving grains exposed outside invites infected rats to contaminate them with their urine and droppings.

question: Which historic code was created after World War II to stop harmful human experiments and protect patient rights?

options.A: The Belmont Report
options.B: The Florence Nightingale Pledge
options.C: The Helsinki Declaration
options.D: The Nuremberg Code

explanation: Spot on! The Nuremberg Code was set up after WWII to make sure human experiments are truly voluntary and safe. You've got this!

question: What is the main focus of emergency nursing?

options.A: Providing long-term physical rehabilitation
options.B: Managing chronic lifestyle diseases at home
options.C: Conducting routine annual health screenings
options.D: Saving lives and stabilizing sudden illnesses

explanation: Emergency nurses specialize in immediate, acute interventions to stabilize patients facing life-threatening situations. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T1#GNS315_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which food group is the best natural source of dietary fiber to promote healthy bowel movements?

options.A: Fatty red meats and processed dairy products
options.B: Processed white bread and refined white rice
options.C: Fresh fruits, vegetables, and whole grains
options.D: Clear sugary beverages and bottled juices

explanation: Plant-based foods and whole grains contain high amounts of natural fiber, which bulks stool and stimulates regular elimination. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T5#GNS212_U1_T5_h6)

question: A patient arrives at the ward with a stab wound to the chest and difficulty breathing. What condition should you suspect?

options.A: Severe bacterial pneumonia
options.B: Chronic bronchitis
options.C: Pneumothorax or hemothorax
options.D: Pulmonary edema from heart failure

explanation: Exactly! Any penetrating chest injury can easily let air or blood into the pleural space, leading to a collapsed lung.

question: Which member of the healthcare team is best at helping a patient relearn everyday tasks like bathing, dressing, and cooking?

options.A: Occupational therapist
options.B: Speech pathologist
options.C: Respiratory therapist
options.D: Physical therapist

explanation: You're doing fantastic! Occupational therapists focus on daily 'occupations'—helping patients gain independence with self-care tasks so they can get back to living their lives.

question: Why is general supportive care often more critical than finding an antidote right away when someone is poisoned?

options.A: Supportive care keeps vital organs working while the body clears the toxin
options.B: Most poisons have strong antidotes available immediately
options.C: Antidotes only work if given within two minutes of exposure
options.D: Antidotes are too expensive to keep in most rural hospitals

explanation: Great thinking! Since we don't have a magical antidote for every single poison out there, keeping the patient's breathing and heart going buys enough time for their body to naturally process and clear the toxin.

question: What type of question should you ask if you want a patient to open up and share their feelings?

options.A: Rhetorical question
options.B: Closed-ended question
options.C: Open-ended question
options.D: Leading question

explanation: Open-ended questions give patients the freedom to talk in their own words, rather than just answering a quick 'yes' or 'no'.

question: In which direction does a pregnant woman's center of gravity shift as her uterus grows?

options.A: Downward
options.B: Backward
options.C: Forward
options.D: Upward

explanation: The growing uterus and fetus pull the body's weight forward, forcing the mother to adjust her posture to avoid falling. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h2)

question: Why do we warm up the small mirror before doing an indirect laryngoscopy?

options.A: To clean off germs
options.B: To keep steam from fogging up the mirror
options.C: To numb the back of the throat so they won't gag
options.D: To widen blood vessels in the throat

explanation: Warm patient breath hitting a cold mirror creates fog. Warming the mirror first keeps the reflection clear so you can see the vocal cords.

question: Why does the fluid inside the semicircular canals move when you quickly turn your head?

options.A: Inertia causing the fluid to momentarily lag behind the moving skull
options.B: Gravity pulling down directly on the fluid particles
options.C: Changes in blood pressure within the temporal bone
options.D: Active contraction of tiny muscles inside the inner ear canal

explanation: Because of inertia, the fluid wants to stay still for a tiny split second, so it sloshes against the moving walls. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T8#GNS211_U4_T8_h3)

question: How fast do chemical buffer systems jump into action when blood pH changes?

options.A: Within fractions of a second
options.B: Over three to five days
options.C: Only when stimulated by the kidneys
options.D: After several hours

explanation: Chemical buffers are the body's fastest responders. They react almost instantly to catch sudden pH changes before other organs even start working.

question: Why must a nurse use a separate measuring cylinder for each patient when emptying drainage bags?

options.A: To stop the plastic containers from wearing out too quickly
options.B: To prevent cross-contamination and spread of infections between patients
options.C: To make measuring the fluid much faster during busy shifts
options.D: To ensure the hospital records look neat and well-organized

explanation: Infection control 101! Using dedicated equipment for every patient keeps germs from hitching a ride across the ward.

question: How do sperm mostly travel upward through the female reproductive tract?

options.A: Riding passively inside the bloodstream after vaginal absorption
options.B: Using their own flagellar motility and uterine muscle contractions
options.C: Crawling along the inner walls using specialized cilia
options.D: Being pushed entirely by gravity when the patient stands

explanation: While sperm use their tails (flagella) to swim, the smooth muscles of the uterus also squeeze rhythmically to help push them along on their journey.

question: What is the most common trigger for autonomic dysreflexia in a hospital ward?

options.A: Eating a high-protein meal too quickly
options.B: Speaking in a loud or stressful voice
options.C: Bladder distension or a blocked urinary catheter
options.D: Sitting in a wheelchair for more than an hour

explanation: A full bladder sends pain signals that get trapped below the spinal injury, triggering a massive, dangerous spike in blood pressure. Always check the catheter first!

question: Why doesn't the mother's immune system treat the growing fetus like a foreign invader and attack it?

options.A: The mother's immune system turns off completely during pregnancy.
options.B: The placenta uses special mechanisms to suppress local maternal immune responses.
options.C: Fetal cells disguise themselves as maternal liver cells.
options.D: The fetus has no white blood cells to trigger an immune reaction.

explanation: Fascinating, right? The placenta acts like a peacekeeper, creating a special low-immune zone so the mother's body doesn't reject the baby.

question: Which type of tummy pain is usually dull, aching, and hard to point to with just one finger?

options.A: Somatic pain
options.B: Visceral pain
options.C: Cutaneous pain
options.D: Neuropathic pain

explanation: When hollow organs stretch or cramp, they cause visceral pain. Because internal organs have fewer pain nerve endings, patients struggle to point to the exact spot.

question: What is the biggest benefit of working hand-in-hand with local leaders during health campaigns?

options.A: They diagnose complex medical conditions in clinics
options.B: They guarantee immediate funding from international donors
options.C: They help dispel cultural myths and reduce resistance
options.D: They replace the need for public health education entirely

explanation: You're right! Local leaders are trusted voices. When they speak up in favor of a health drive, community members feel much safer and more willing to listen.

question: A healthy child receives a routine measles vaccine at the local health clinic. What type of immunity is being stimulated?

options.A: Natural passive immunity
options.B: Natural active immunity
options.C: Artificial passive immunity
options.D: Artificial active immunity

explanation: Vaccines introduce weakened or dead pathogen parts to trigger the body to make its own antibodies, which is artificial active immunity. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h3)

question: What happens when a hospital collects survey feedback from nurses but never actually changes anything?

options.A: Turnover rates drop because staff appreciate being asked
options.B: The hospital saves money on administrative overhead
options.C: Employee motivation automatically increases anyway
options.D: Staff develop cynicism and lose trust in leadership

explanation: If staff share their struggles and nothing changes, they stop caring and lose trust in management. Actions speak louder than surveys!

question: What is a major benefit of Tai Chi for older adults at risk of falling?

options.A: It rapidly increases total body bone density
options.B: It improves balance through slow, controlled movements
options.C: It eliminates the need for any assistive devices
options.D: It cures chronic joint inflammation in the knees

explanation: Tai Chi trains neuromuscular control and core stability, making it one of the most effective exercises for fall prevention. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T5#GNS324_U6_T5_h5)

question: What is the primary function of luteinizing hormone in the male reproductive system?

options.A: Stimulating testosterone production in the testes
options.B: Directly forming the flagellum of maturing sperm
options.C: Neutralizing acidic fluid in the male urethra
options.D: Lowering body temperature inside the scrotal sac

explanation: Luteinizing hormone targets specific cells in the testes to trigger the synthesis and release of testosterone. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h3)

question: Why might someone with diabetes and failing kidneys suddenly need less insulin than before?

options.A: Damaged kidneys fail to clear circulating insulin from the blood
options.B: Muscle tissue begins burning glucose much faster than normal
options.C: The liver stops storing glucose as glycogen
options.D: The pancreas suddenly starts producing extra insulin on its own

explanation: Brilliant! Healthy kidneys normally help clear out used insulin. When they are damaged, insulin hangs around in the blood longer, meaning you need less injected insulin.

question: What is the main job of haemostasis in the human body?

options.A: To increase blood pressure during shock
options.B: To speed up the flow of red blood cells
options.C: To stop bleeding after a vessel gets injured
options.D: To destroy unwanted bacteria in the blood

explanation: Think of haemostasis as your body's natural emergency repair team! Its main job is to stop bleeding and patch up damaged blood vessels.

question: When gathering supplies to make an empty bed, where is the safest place to put your clean linen stack?

options.A: On a clean bedside chair, never on another patient's bed
options.B: Directly on the clean floor to keep your hands free
options.C: Held tightly against your uniform while walking
options.D: Stacked on top of the patient's meal tray for easy reach

explanation: Spot on! Keeping clean linen on a chair or clean table stops it from picking up germs from the floor or other units.

question: Which question is a patient in the anger stage most likely to ask?

options.A: How much will this treatment cost?
options.B: When will my test results arrive?
options.C: Can we negotiate more time?
options.D: Why is this happening to me?

explanation: Anger comes from deep hurt and the feeling of unfairness, making patients ask 'Why me?'

question: What visual sign immediately confirms a successful intradermal PPD injection?

options.A: A flat red rash spreading on the arm
options.B: A small droplet of bright red blood
options.C: Immediate bruising around the needle
options.D: A pale raised skin bleb or wheal

explanation: A proper intradermal injection creates a distinct bump or wheal on the skin surface, showing the fluid is trapped in the correct layer. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h4)

question: Why must nurses treat used clinical items as places where germs actively grow?

options.A: Because hospital trash is legally classified as hazardous material automatically
options.B: Because cleaning staff refuse to handle items unless they are labeled alive
options.C: Because used items contain moisture and nutrients that help microbes multiply
options.D: Because all discarded items will immediately begin to emit toxic gases

explanation: Spot on! Things like used dressings and body fluids provide a warm, wet home full of nutrients. Germs love this and will multiply rapidly if we don't contain them properly.

question: How does a lethargic patient usually act during an assessment?

options.A: Completely unresponsive even to painful stimuli
options.B: Fully awake and answers every question instantly
options.C: Aggressive and physically combative with staff
options.D: Drowsy and drifts off to sleep when not stimulated

explanation: A lethargic patient wakes up when you talk to them or touch them, but they tend to drift right back off to sleep the moment you stop interacting.

question: Which type of white blood cell is most dominant in acute inflammation?

options.A: Eosinophils
options.B: Basophils
options.C: Neutrophils
options.D: Lymphocytes

explanation: Neutrophils are the first responders that rush to the site of an acute injury. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is Chadwick's sign?

options.A: A bluish discoloration of the vagina and cervix
options.B: A softening of the lower uterine segment
options.C: The fluttering sensation of fetal movement
options.D: A softening of service tip

explanation: Chadwick's sign is that distinct bluish-violet tint in the vaginal walls caused by extra blood rushing to the area during pregnancy.

question: What is a primary responsibility of community health nurses regarding food security?

options.A: Inspecting the mechanical engines of commercial cargo vehicles
options.B: Identifying nutritional deficits and educating vulnerable families
options.C: Setting international market prices for agricultural crops
options.D: Driving heavy trucks to transport harvests from farms to cities

explanation: Nurses assess nutritional health at the grassroots level and teach communities how to make the best use of available foods. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T025#GNS227_U2_T025_h8)

question: When the inner lining of blood vessels gets damaged in preeclampsia, what is the main result?

options.A: Damaged kidney tissues heal rapidly
options.B: Blood vessels squeeze tight and leak fluid
options.C: Massive production of red blood cells
options.D: Uterine muscles permanently relax

explanation: Think of the blood vessels as having tiny leaks. When they get damaged, they tighten up and let fluid seep into body tissues, causing high BP and swelling.

question: What is the main goal of a community's 'production, distribution, and consumption' function?

options.A: Providing free hospital care to every citizen
options.B: Teaching cultural values to children in school buildings
options.C: Enforcing criminal laws and maintaining local police stations
options.D: Meeting the basic survival and economic needs of members

explanation: You've got it! This is simply about making sure people have access to food, shelter, and the basics needed to survive every day.

question: What is the main mindset shift behind trauma-informed care?

options.A: Asking what happened to the patient instead of what is wrong with them
options.B: Minimizing emotional expressions to maintain clinical efficiency
options.C: Determining the legal guilt of the alleged perpetrator immediately
options.D: Focusing exclusively on surgical repair of physical wounds

explanation: Instead of judging a patient's behavior, trauma-informed care reminds us to ask, 'What happened to you?' It's all about empathy.

question: What is a major social barrier that prevents Nigerian teenagers from seeking care?

options.A: Fear of community gossip and moral judgment from adults
options.B: Excessive availability of youth-only private hospitals everywhere
options.C: Mandatory free transport provided by local government councils
options.D: Strict laws requiring teenagers to study nursing in secondary school

explanation: Cultural stigma and the fear of being judged or gossiped about in the community stop many young people from visiting clinics. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T4#GNS312_U4_T4_h3)

question: Why is keeping strict privacy and confidentiality so important when teenagers come in for reproductive health services?

options.A: It removes the need to document clinical findings in health records
options.B: It is a legal requirement only for adult patients, not minors
options.C: It builds trust and encourages teens to seek necessary medical advice early
options.D: It prevents parents from ever knowing their child is growing up

explanation: You got it! Teens are often scared of being judged. Promising confidentiality helps them feel safe enough to get help before small issues turn big.

question: Which clinical finding during a routine physical checkup might first alert a nurse to the presence of past FGM?

options.A: Enlarged thyroid gland in the neck
options.B: Spontaneous bruising on the upper extremities
options.C: Unexplained scarring and altered anatomy of the external genitalia
options.D: Asymmetrical deep tendon reflexes in the lower limbs

explanation: Visual inspection during relevant examinations often reveals missing structures or dense scar tissue characteristic of previous mutilation. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h6)

question: If a patient has their entire pituitary gland surgically removed, which of these medications do they NOT need to take for the rest of their life?

options.A: Thyroid hormone replacement
options.B: Sex hormone replacement
options.C: Cortisol replacement (glucocorticoids)
options.D: Insulin injections

explanation: Insulin is made by your pancreas, not your pituitary gland! Without a pituitary, the patient will need lifelong thyroid, adrenal, and sex hormone replacements, but their pancreas keeps making insulin just fine.

question: A patient on warfarin asks if they can take routine ibuprofen for joint pain. What should you tell them?

options.A: Only take ibuprofen if you crush the tablets into powder first
options.B: Substitute ibuprofen with local herbal mixtures to avoid side effects
options.C: No, ibuprofen can interact with your treatment and greatly increase your risk of bleeding
options.D: Yes, ibuprofen is completely safe to combine with any blood-thinning medication

explanation: NSAIDs like ibuprofen irritate the stomach lining and mess with platelets. Combined with warfarin, it's a fast track to dangerous bleeding!

question: Why must work inside the TSSU always flow in one direction?

options.A: To reduce the electricity consumption of heavy sterilizing machines
options.B: To prevent clean and sterile items from mixing with dirty ones
options.C: To make it easier for nursing students to clean the floors
options.D: To speed up the physical movement of heavy instrument trays

explanation: Exactly! Keeping a one-way workflow ensures items only move forward from dirty to clean, protecting patients from cross-contamination.

question: What is the main way beta-blockers help the heart?

options.A: Blocking the reabsorption of sodium in the renal tubules
options.B: Decreasing heart rate and force of myocardial contraction
options.C: Triggering rapid constriction of peripheral blood vessels
options.D: Stimulating the release of renin directly from the kidneys

explanation: Exactly! Beta-blockers tell the heart to slow down and beat a bit softer, giving overworked heart muscle a much-needed rest.

question: What is a core goal of immunization within Primary Health Care?

options.A: To treat acute bacterial infections in children
options.B: To replace the need for clean water and nutrition
options.C: To interrupt transmission of vaccine-preventable diseases
options.D: To completely eliminate all known human illnesses

explanation: The main purpose of immunization in public health is to prevent specific infectious diseases and stop them from spreading in communities. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h1)

question: Which phase of cancer development involves a permanent change or mutation in a cell's DNA?

options.A: Initiation
options.B: Progression
options.C: Metastasis
options.D: Promotion

explanation: You nailed it! Initiation is always step one—it's the very first moment a trigger causes a permanent genetic change in a normal cell.

question: Which part of the nervous system lets you consciously control your skeletal muscles to walk or write?

options.A: Sympathetic nervous system
options.B: Somatic nervous system
options.C: Autonomic nervous system
options.D: Parasympathetic nervous system

explanation: The somatic system handles voluntary movements—the things you decide to do on purpose. Keep pushing forward! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T2#GNS211_U3_T2_h5)

question: What drives the extremely fast skin cell growth seen in plaque psoriasis?

options.A: Cold weather triggers massive mast cell breakdown
options.B: The body attacks and destroys pigment cells in the base layer
options.C: Bacteria directly eat away at the outer skin layer
options.D: T-cells release chemical signals that speed up skin cell division

explanation: In psoriasis, hyperactive T-cells release inflammatory chemicals that tell skin cells to multiply way too fast, piling up into those thick, silvery scales.

question: What is the biggest downside to using benzodiazepines over a long period?

options.A: They carry a high risk of tolerance and physical dependence.
options.B: They cause severe weight loss in all patients.
options.C: They permanently destroy brain neurotransmitters.
options.D: They take at least six weeks to start working.

explanation: Benzodiazepines work fast, which is great for quick relief. But the body gets used to them quickly, leading to addiction and dependency if used long-term.

question: Which room setup is most important when getting ready for a physical exam?

options.A: Bright flashing lights for visibility
options.B: A cold room temperature to prevent sweating
options.C: Adequate privacy and good lighting
options.D: Open doors to encourage fresh airflow

explanation: Good lighting helps you see subtle skin changes clearly, and privacy helps your patient relax and feel secure with you. Always set the stage for comfort!

question: Which combination of symptoms is a major red flag for a postpartum uterine infection?

options.A: Mild swelling in both ankles
options.B: Foul-smelling lochia and fever
options.C: Gradual lightening of lochia color
options.D: Increased appetite and energy

explanation: Spot on! Fever combined with lower tummy pain and bad-smelling lochia are classic signs that the uterus might be infected and needs medical attention.

question: What usually blocks the sinuses and triggers a painful sinus infection after a common cold?

options.A: Rupture of the tympanic membrane from high pressure
options.B: Obstruction of the sinus ostia due to mucosal swelling
options.C: Paralysis of the vocal cords in the larynx
options.D: Direct bacterial destruction of the inner ear bones

explanation: When your nasal tissues swell up from a cold, they block the tiny drainage holes (ostia) of your sinuses. This traps mucus inside, making it a cozy home for bacteria to grow. You're mastering this!

question: Which tools do clinics primarily use to track when a family planning client is due back?

options.A: Daily weather monitoring charts
options.B: Appointment registers and individual client cards
options.C: Pharmacy inventory bills for unrelated drugs
options.D: National television broadcast schedules

explanation: Client cards and clinic registers are our best friends for keeping track of return dates so no one slips through the cracks.

question: As a nurse, what is a major safety risk you must watch out for in patients with advanced Parkinson's disease?

options.A: Aspiration due to swallowing difficulties
options.B: Spontaneous regeneration of nerve tissue
options.C: Sudden permanent paralysis of the lower limbs
options.D: Excessive weight gain from hyperactive metabolism

explanation: Swallowing problems (dysphagia) are very common in late-stage Parkinson's. If food or saliva goes down the 'wrong pipe', it can lead to dangerous chest infections or choking.

question: A patient suddenly feels intense terror, chest pain, and a sense of doom that peaks within minutes. What condition matches this?

options.A: Generalized anxiety disorder
options.B: Social anxiety disorder
options.C: Specific phobia
options.D: Panic disorder

explanation: Exactly! Those sudden, terrifying rushes with strong physical signs are classic hallmarks of panic attacks seen in panic disorder.

question: What is the proper way to fix a writing error on a paper nursing chart?

options.A: Tear out the entire page and rewrite the nursing notes
options.B: Draw a single line through the error and write your initials
options.C: Scratch out the wrong words until they disappear
options.D: Cover the mistake completely with thick correction fluid

explanation: Well done! Drawing a single line keeps the original words readable while showing it was corrected, preventing any look of tampering.

question: A patient has been on strict bed rest for several weeks. What is likely happening to their bones?

options.A: Calcium storage in the bones is doubling
options.B: Bone-building cells are rapidly making the bones thicker
options.C: Bone breakdown (resorption) is happening faster than bone building
options.D: Spongy bone is turning into solid metal-like columns

explanation: Bones love movement and weight! Without that daily mechanical stress, the bone-builders slow down, letting the breakdown cells take over and weaken the bone density.

question: Which organs serve as the primary sites where immune cells are produced and mature?

options.A: Kidneys and ureters
options.B: Liver and gallbladder
options.C: Spleen and lymph nodes
options.D: Bone marrow and thymus

explanation: Primary immune organs like the bone marrow and thymus are responsible for the generation and maturation of vital immune cells. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h1)

question: Why is malaria considered an endemic disease in Nigeria?

options.A: Because transmission cycles happen year-round without stopping
options.B: Because it causes sudden outbreaks only during the harmattan season
options.C: Because the federal government eradicated it completely last year
options.D: Because it only affects individuals who travel outside the country

explanation: Malaria remains present at predictable, steady rates in Nigeria throughout the entire year, which is the exact definition of an endemic disease.

question: What does a high waist circumference mostly tell you about a patient's health risk?

options.A: Severe protein deficiency and muscle wasting
options.B: A normal and healthy distribution of total body water
options.C: Excess visceral fat linked to heart disease and diabetes
options.D: Chronic lung disease and poor oxygen exchange

explanation: Fat stored around the belly and internal organs is strongly linked to a higher risk of heart problems and diabetes. Excellent clinical insight!

question: Why are finger foods so helpful for patients with advanced dementia during meals?

options.A: It prevents the patient from spilling liquids on their hospital gown
options.B: It guarantees the patient will eat three full meals every single day
options.C: It promotes independence and makes eating easier for confused patients
options.D: It eliminates the need for any nursing staff supervision

explanation: Spot on! When handling cutlery gets confusing, finger foods let patients feed themselves and hold onto their dignity.

question: Why do nurses say that pain is a subjective experience?

options.A: It disappears completely as soon as vital signs return to normal.
